brewing.notes: A safe starting point for raw pu-erh: rinse once, gongfu style, short early steeps.

description:
Midi, also called Midi tribute tea, comes from an ancient tea mountain in Xinfu Township, Mojiang County, Yunnan.

Treat it as you would any raw pu-erh: rinse the leaf, keep early steeps short, and ask which year and which trees it comes from, since village names on Yunnan teas are often stretched.
history: The gardens lie at 1300 to 1940 m, with a mean yearly temperature of 14.2 to 18.3 °C, about 1293 mm of annual rain and red and yellow-brown soils. One spring price listing puts it at 1200 to 2500 yuan per kilogram. Little more is documented, including how it earned the tribute name.
processing: Typical of raw pu-erh: sun-dried large-leaf mao cha, usually steamed and stone-pressed, then left to age slowly.
harvest_season: Usually spring leaf is prized, as with most raw pu-erh.
appearance_dry: Usually a pressed cake of silvery-green to brown leaf, darkening with age.
appearance_liquor: Usually pale gold when young, deepening to amber with age.
taste_profile: Pronounced bitterness and astringency that turn sweet quickly, with a clear fragrance, a faint orchid note and an evident wild character.
vintage_note: Raw pu-erh is sold by harvest year: young at 1 to 3 years, mid-aged at 5 to 10, aged at 15 or more. Storage matters as much as age.
